notes: Blind design course (honest instruments): deliverable is docs/status/honest-instruments-ideal.md. Key choices: (1) the property 'every reading is known, unknown, or refused' is enforced by ONE mechanism — a tri-state reading type at every emission boundary, with Measured unconstructible without provenance and Unknown/Refused unconstructible without a reason; parsing strictness, fold-derived counters, birth-time identity, and expiring liveness claims are framed as four applications of that single type, not four mechanisms. (2) Conformance contract stated as seven clauses (C1 trivalence, C2 provenance, C3 refusal of unrecognised input, C4 derived counts, C5 birth-time identity, C6 expiring claims, C7 falsifiable checks), each with an explicit yes/no inspection procedure so conformance is decidable by inspection. (3) The vacuous-checker class ('a check that cannot fail') is addressed by a meta-test policy: committed known-good/known-bad fixtures exercised through the check's real code path, the suite asserting the known-bad fixture FAILS (so a cannot-fail check breaks the build), periodic mutation probes against historically observed defect classes, and impossibly-clean counters treated as suspect rather than reassuring. (4) Deliberate omissions recorded: confidence scores, auto-repair/retry, cryptographic tamper-evidence, fuzzy auto-correction, central honesty monitor, tolerance shims — each with the reason. (5) Costs named: Unknown-handling verbosity, strict-refusal UX breakage, doubled fixture maintenance, lease-horizon tuning, recompute-at-report-time cost, all-or-nothing per-surface adoption.
